questions.stem: Which of the following is the most important principle to maintain during any surgical procedure?
options: A. Rapid closure of the wound
B. Adequate hemostasis
C. Use of the largest possible instruments
D. Avoidance of all antibiotics
questions.explanation: Adequate hemostasis prevents postoperative bleeding and infection; it is a fundamental surgical principle. Rapid closure, instrument size, and blanket avoidance of antibiotics are not primary concerns.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most important principle to maintain during the surgical removal of a tumour to prevent dissemination of malignant cells?
options: A. Use of cold scissors
B. Gentle handling of the tumour
C. Immediate postoperative radiotherapy
D. Administration of high-dose steroids
questions.explanation: Gentle handling of the tumour (option B) is the key principle to avoid tumour spillage and local recurrence. Cold scissors are not a recognized technique for this purpose, postoperative radiotherapy and steroids do not prevent intraoperative dissemination.

questions.stem: A 45‑year‑old man presents with a 2‑week history of progressive abdominal distension and constipation. Examination reveals a firm, non‑tender mass in the left upper quadrant. Imaging shows a large, well‑encapsulated cystic lesion arising from the splenic hilum. Which of the following is the most appropriate first step in management?
options: A. Immediate exploratory laparotomy
B. Percutaneous fine‑needle aspiration under imaging guidance
C. Observation with serial abdominal ultrasounds
D. Endoscopic ultrasound‑guided drainage
questions.explanation: The lesion is a large, well‑encapsulated cystic mass arising from the splenic hilum, most consistent with a splenic cyst or pseudocyst. The safest and most definitive first step is immediate exploratory laparotomy with possible splenectomy or cystectomy, as the mass is large and symptomatic. Percutaneous aspiration is contraindicated in cystic lesions of the spleen due to risk of rupture and infection, and observation would delay definitive treatment. Endoscopic drainage is not applicable for a splenic mass.
questions.source: Principles of surgical management of cystic splenic lesions

questions.stem: A 68‑year‑old man presents with a large, exophytic, ulcerated lesion on the left flank. Imaging shows a 12 cm mass arising from the left adrenal gland with invasion of the adjacent kidney and a small area of pulmonary nodules. The patient is otherwise medically fit. Which of the following statements best reflects the current surgical principle for management of this tumour?
options: A. Perform a staged approach with initial adrenalectomy followed by nephrectomy and later metastasectomy
B. Undertake a single‑stage en bloc resection of the adrenal gland, kidney, and involved retroperitoneal tissue, followed by adjuvant chemotherapy
C. Opt for palliative debulking surgery to relieve pain, deferring systemic therapy
D. Rely on stereotactic body radiotherapy alone, as surgery offers no survival benefit in metastatic adrenal carcinoma
questions.explanation: The optimal surgical principle for a locally advanced adrenal carcinoma with limited metastatic disease is a single‑stage en bloc resection of all involved organs (adrenal, kidney, retroperitoneum) to achieve negative margins, followed by adjuvant systemic therapy. Staged surgery (option A) risks tumour seeding and delays definitive treatment. Palliative debulking (option C) is reserved for unresectable disease. Stereotactic radiotherapy (option D) is not the standard of care for primary adrenal carcinoma with local invasion.
questions.source: Principle of en bloc resection in locally advanced adrenal carcinoma

questions.stem: A 45‑year‑old man presents with a 3‑month history of intermittent right upper quadrant pain, nausea, and a palpable mass in the right hypochondrium. Imaging shows a 6‑cm cystic lesion arising from the gallbladder with irregular thickening of the cyst wall and focal calcifications. Which of the following statements best reflects the most appropriate surgical management of this lesion?
options: A. Elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy with intra‑operative frozen section of the cyst wall
B. Open cholecystectomy with en bloc resection of the cyst and adjacent liver segments 4b and 5
C. Percutaneous drainage of the cyst followed by observation
D. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) with sphincterotomy and stent placement
questions.explanation: The imaging findings are highly suspicious for gallbladder carcinoma arising within a cystic lesion. The standard of care is an open cholecystectomy with en bloc resection of the involved liver segments (usually segments 4b and 5) to achieve negative margins. Laparoscopic removal alone (option A) carries a risk of tumor spillage and incomplete resection. Percutaneous drainage (option C) is inappropriate for a malignant cystic mass, and ERCP (option D) is not therapeutic for gallbladder carcinoma.
questions.source: Principles of Surgical Oncology – Gallbladder Cancer
